**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT).**

- **Problem:** § 22.1 (p0093) allows Vendor to "audit Customer at any time without notice" and to "remotely access Customer's systems and records" — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote system access, which is walk-away territory under the rule and fails even the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, no system access). It also directly contradicts § 22.2, which bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems.
- **Already acceptable:** § 22.2 puts audit cost on Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent and restricts scope; § 22.3 makes findings Customer Confidential Information. Both meet the preferred position, so no edits there.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** § 22.1 replaced with a once-per-twelve-months limit, 30 days' prior written notice, normal business hours, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality at least as protective as § 16, and no access to Customer systems — with 15 days' notice offered as a fallback in the comment.
